detail.body:
## Summary

This PR adds MoonEP virtual-expert load balancing over HybridEP (`--moe-virtual-expert-load-balance`).


Requirements and limitations (no FSDP, variable sequence lengths, capacity factor, expert bias, sinkhorn, partial MoE CUDA-graph scopes, or FC1 offload) are documented in the [MoE README](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/README.md#virtual-expert-load-balancing).

## Architecture

Each rank exposes 2·L runtime experts to HybridEP: its L native experts plus L virtual slots. HybridEP itself is unmodified. It receives the planner's runtime expert IDs and a fixed worst-case capacity ([load_balancer:L805-812](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L805-L812)).

The new code is the kernels in `virtual_expert_triton.py`, the runtime in `virtual_expert_load_balancer.py`, and glue in the dispatcher, router, experts, TE, GTP, and config (see [Per-file changes](#per-file-changes)).

## Load balancer design

[`virtual_expert_load_balancer.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L1-L965) is the runtime between the kernels and Megatron.

- **On the first forward**, it creates a shared symmetric-memory workspace used across every iteration:
  - one weight arena and one grad arena per expert layout, exposed as virtual-slot weights. All layers with the same layout share the same arenas, so the slots hold one layer's replicas at a time and each layer's forward and backward push refills them;
  - the slots are bound into TE's grouped GEMM alongside the natives but kept invisible to DDP, the optimizer, and checkpointing;
  - pointer tables that fix every weight and grad address from then on.
- **On each iteration**, it:
  - plans the layer's routes and pushes the selected weights into peer slots on side streams;
  - lets HybridEP and TE run over natives plus slots;
  - in the backward, pushes again, reduces the slot gradients back into the owners' native `main_grad` (or GTP's wgrad scratch), and hands the result to DDP or GTP;
  - has the compute stream wait on events at the points listed in the Integration table.
- **With GTP**, it reaches GTP through TE's `DistributedWeight` interface rather than by special-casing GTP inside TE.

### Structures

- [`VirtualExpertLoadBalancer`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L587-L965): the mixin the dispatcher inherits, so the HybridEP transport itself stays untouched. It does the first-forward setup, owns the side streams and events, and runs the per-iteration steps above by launching the kernels and attaching the hooks.
- [`_VirtualExpertStorage`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L126-L293): the shared workspace, one per expert layout, holding a weight arena and a grad arena in NCCL symmetric memory so peers can write and read them directly. Each slot is exposed as a weight whose gradient buffer is a view of the grad arena, which is what the kernels push into and reduce from.
- [`_VirtualExperts`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L448-L561): one layer's view of that workspace. It builds the weight list TE sees (natives then slots), keeps the pointer tables that the kernels read and that must stay fixed, and at the end of the backward hands the native gradients to DDP.
- [`_GTPTEWeightBridge`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L304-L445): the GTP variant of that view. With expert GTP the native weights are gathered per forward and the wgrads reduce-scattered, so this class implements TE's `DistributedWeight` interface to obtain the gathered weights before the push and to delay the reduce-scatter until the slot gradients have arrived.
- [`VirtualExpertPlan`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L71-L85): one forward's plan (runtime IDs and which experts to copy) and its in-flight state. It is kept until that forward's backward finishes, so interleaved microbatches and repeated MTP forwards each keep their own.
- [`_VirtualExpertHook`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L567-L580): the identity autograd function that triggers the backward steps (see Integration). It passes its tensor through unchanged and runs a load-balancer method when the gradient reaches it.

## Kernel design

The three kernels are designed to run fast and to overlap with HybridEP and expert compute on side streams:

- **No host syncs**
  - The CPU never waits on the GPU, because all sizes are static and the plan stays on the device. This keeps launches asynchronous and makes the kernels CUDA-graph capturable.
- **Deterministic**
  - The planner breaks ties with a fixed rule and keeps route order within each expert, so every rank computes the same plan.
  - The grad reduce sums in a fixed order and rounds once, so results are bitwise reproducible.
- **Small, fixed grids**
  - All kernels use at most 32 SMs, leaving the rest for the overlapped attention and shared-expert compute.
- **Static shapes and pointers**
  - Pointer tables are built once and checked on every later pass.

All three kernels are single cooperative launches in `virtual_expert_triton.py`.

For the two transport kernels, regular NCCL isn't sufficient because the plan lives on the device:

- send/recv needs each peer and byte count on the host, which would force a device-to-host sync per layer;
- a dense all-to-all or reduce-scatter over every expert slot would avoid that sync but move up to EP× more data.

Instead, both kernels read `experts_to_copy` on the device and access the peers' symmetric memory directly.

### Planner ([`_plan_virtual_expert_routes_kernel`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L135-L425))

The planner runs the MoonEP algorithm on the router output. Its inputs are the router's top-k expert IDs `[T, topk]` (int32/int64), the token alignment from `get_align_size_for_quantization` (256, because MoonEP requires TE grouped tensors), and a [planner workspace](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L453-L498) holding the symmetric histogram window and scratch space.

It produces two tensors:

- the MoonEP-adjusted routing map: runtime expert IDs `[T, topk]` int16 that HybridEP dispatches to;
- `experts_to_copy` `[EP, L]` int32: the experts each rank must copy into its slots ([triton:L501-550](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L501-L550)).

Everything runs in a single 32-block launch, in this order:

1. **Local histogram** ([triton:L193-202](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L193-L202)): each block counts the routes in a contiguous range of tokens. The block's row is kept so that route order can be recovered in step 7.
2. **Cross-rank exchange** ([triton:L205-231](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L205-L231)): each rank writes its histogram into every peer's symmetric-memory window, followed by one rendezvous. After this, every rank holds every rank's histogram.
3. **Global expert load** ([triton:L237-277](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L237-L277)): sum the histograms to get the global route count of each expert, and from that the total load of each rank. Each expert's count is rounded up to the alignment once, so placement works in aligned blocks ([triton:L254-256](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L254-L256)).
4. **Pair senders with receivers** ([triton:L293-311](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L293-L311)): repeatedly pair the most-loaded rank with the emptiest one. The receiver takes its whole deficit from that single sender, which guarantees L slots are always enough.
5. **Split each sender's quota across its experts** ([triton:L312-345](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L312-L345)): the largest remaining expert fills the largest remaining quota. This gives the cumulative route boundaries for each destination.
6. **Assign slots** ([triton:L349-367](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L349-L367)): each receiver puts its incoming experts into slots 0..L−1 and writes `experts_to_copy`.
7. **Remap routes** ([triton:L371-424](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L371-L424)): compute stable per-expert ordinals from earlier blocks' histograms plus an in-tile sort ([triton:L393-407](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L393-L407)). A binary search over the boundaries then picks each route's destination and runtime ID ([triton:L410-424](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L410-L424)). Routes for the same expert keep their order.

### Weight push ([`_virtual_expert_weight_push_kernel`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L708-L769))

This kernel copies local expert weights into the virtual slots of peer GPUs in the expert-parallel group, following the planner's `experts_to_copy` ([launcher](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L949-L1001)). It runs before the forward expert GEMMs and again before the backward ones, because the slots are shared across layers and get overwritten in between.

- **Who sends what:** each owner picks out the entries of `experts_to_copy` that name its own experts, so it sends only the experts some peer actually needs ([triton:L743-748](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L743-L748)).
- **Work split:** each expert copy is cut into segments and spread across the blocks. Blocks working at the same time are given different destination peers, so the transfer uses every NVLink at once instead of queuing on one ([triton:L672-682](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L672-L682)).
- **Copy path:** the weights are read locally and written into the peer's arena as raw bytes, so BF16 and MXFP8 (data and scales) are copied unchanged ([triton:L684-704](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L684-L704)).
- **Barrier:** one on exit, so every slot is filled before any rank starts its expert GEMMs ([triton:L769](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L769)).

### Grad reduce ([`_virtual_expert_grad_reduce_kernel`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L785-L899))

After the backward GEMMs, each virtual slot holds a partial gradient for an expert that belongs to another rank. This kernel brings those partials home: each owner reads the slot gradients from every peer that hosted one of its experts and adds them into its own expert gradient ([launcher](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L1004-L1055)). It runs twice per layer, once for FC2 right after FC2's weight-gradient GEMM and once for FC1 after dispatch backward, so each can overlap the rest of the backward ([load_balancer:L915-936](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L915-L936)).

- **Who reads from whom:** the planner's `experts_to_copy` tells each owner which peers hold copies of its experts, so only those slots are read ([triton:L839-849](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L839-L849)).
- **Peer reads:** one TMA descriptor covers every peer's grad arena ([triton:L855-862](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L855-L862)). This works because symmetric memory places all peers' arenas at the same stride, which the host checks once ([load_balancer:L178-187](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L178-L187)).
- **Accumulation:** for each tile, the owner's own gradient and the peer partials are summed in FP32 in a fixed order and written once ([triton:L873-898](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L873-L898)). The result is bitwise identical from run to run, which a NCCL reduce-scatter would not guarantee.
- **Barriers:** one on entry, so every peer has finished writing its slot gradients, and one on exit, so every owner has finished reading and the slots can be reused ([triton:L863](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L863), [triton:L899](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L899)).

### Synchronization primitives

We create synchronization primitives to order symmetric-memory reads and writes across ranks, since no NCCL collective does this for us.

- **[`_grid_sync`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L99-L112)**: a self-resetting grid barrier. Block 0 flips a tag bit and each block waits for the flip, so no reset is needed between launches.
- **[`_rendezvous`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L581-L607)**: one int32 flag per ordered rank pair in the symmetric signal pad ([triton:L553-578](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L553-L578)). A release-flip to every peer is followed by an acquire-consume from every peer. The flags reset themselves.
- **[`_cross_rank_barrier`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L610-L638)**: a grid sync, then a block-0 rendezvous, then another grid sync and a proxy fence so later TMA reads see the peer writes.
  - In the push, the exit barrier means the slots are filled before anyone computes.
  - In the reduce, the entry barrier means every peer's wgrad is written, and the exit barrier means the slots can be reused.
- **[Timeouts](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L67-L96)**: every wait polls `globaltimer` and traps after ~100 s, even with `TRITON_DEBUG=0`. This turns a hang into a CUDA error. The planner's device asserts only fire with `TRITON_DEBUG=1`.

## Integration of MoonEP with the MoE layer

MoonEP launches three kernels per layer on side streams, each of which has to run at a specific point in the forward or backward:

- **Planner**: runs after the router and must finish before dispatch.
- **Weight push**: runs once before the forward expert GEMMs and again before the backward expert GEMMs, because the slots are shared and get overwritten between passes.
- **Gradient reduction**: runs after each FC's wgrad GEMM and must finish before the gradients are handed to DDP or GTP.

The forward calls these kernels directly. In the backward, they are triggered by identity [`_VirtualExpertHook`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L567-L580)s placed on four forward tensors (the layer input, the dispatch input, the combine input, and the layer output), plus a forward pre-hook on FC1 and FC2's `wgrad_store`. The input hook takes the real parameters as extra inputs ([`wrap_layer_input`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L816-L823)), and this is the only autograd edge back to them.

The table below lists each trigger. Read the forward column top to bottom and the backward column bottom to top.

| Step | Code | Forward | Backward |
|---|---|---|---|
| layer input | [`MoELayer.route`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L523) → [`wrap_layer_input`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L816-L823) | On the first call, size the capacity and bind the runtime weights ([`_runtime_init`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L658-L754)); attach the input hook | Wait for both reductions, zero the slot grads (non-GTP), then hand native grads to DDP (dummy grads fire its hooks) or run the deferred GTP reduce-scatter ([`_finish_grad_reduce`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L951-L965)) |
| router | [`TopKRouter.routing`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L997-L1045) | Emit compact `[T, topk]` expert IDs and probs | |
| preprocess | [`_VirtualExpertHybridEPManager.setup_metadata`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py#L1352-L1368) → [`plan_dispatch`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L830-L836) | Launch the planner on `planner_stream`, then the forward weight push on `weight_stream` | |
| shared experts | [`MoELayer.forward`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L740-L752) (reordered) | Run after preprocess so they overlap with the planner and push | |
| dispatch | [`_VirtualExpertHybridEPManager.dispatch`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py#L1370-L1390) → [`prepare_virtual_expert_dispatch`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L838-L852) | Wait for the planner, scatter probs onto the planner's runtime IDs, run HybridEP dispatch with the fixed worst-case capacity; attach the dispatch hook | Launch the FC1 reduction on `grad_stream` (and FC2 if it hasn't started), overlapping router/shared-expert backward |
| expert FC1 | `linear_fc1` forward pre-hook ([registered in `_runtime_init`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L751-L754)) | Wait for the forward push before the first expert GEMM ([`_wait_weight_push`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L888-L895)) | |
| expert FC2 | [`linear_fc2.wgrad_store.put`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py#L237-L261) (non-GTP) / [`finalize_group_grads`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L411-L420) (GTP) | | Run the FC2 wgrad GEMM, then immediately launch the FC2 reduction so it overlaps FC1 backward |
| combine | [`_VirtualExpertHybridEPManager.combine`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py#L1392-L1405) → [`prepare_virtual_expert_combine`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L854-L856) | Attach the combine hook | Wait for the backward push and bind the DDP grad pointers before the expert backward GEMMs ([`_prepare_expert_backward`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L906-L909)) |
| layer output | [`MoELayer.forward`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L694) → [`finalize_layer_output`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L858-L862) | Move the plan into the output hook's context; attach the hook | Restore the plan and launch the backward weight push (slots may have been overwritten by other layers) ([`_start_backward`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py#L898-L903)) |

The plan is stored in the output hook's context, so each microbatch and each MTP forward keeps its own plan.

## Per-file changes

Each entry says why the file had to change, then what changed.

### `megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py` (new)

**Why:** the planner, weight push, and gradient reduce need custom kernels; see [Kernel design](#kernel-design).

**What changed:** new file.
- [`VirtualExpertPlannerWorkspace`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L453-L498) owns the histogram window and scratch space the planner writes into. Compiled planner launches are cached per shape so later layers don't pay the Triton dispatch cost ([cache key](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L519-L549)).
- Kernel launches go through [`_launch_with_descriptor_allocator`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_triton.py#L938-L946), which scopes Triton's descriptor allocator to the launch. This is why Triton 3.5 or newer is required.

### `megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py` (new)

**Why:** something has to connect the kernels to autograd, streams, and parameter storage; see [Load balancer design](#load-balancer-design).

**What changed:** new file. It is a mixin, so the HybridEP transport is left untouched and the virtual slots never become optimizer or checkpoint state.

### `megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py`

**Why:** MoonEP has to plug into the flex dispatcher, and HybridEP has to accept a capacity that the planner computed rather than one derived from a capacity factor.

**What changed:**
- A new HybridEP subclass, [`_VirtualExpertHybridEPManager`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py#L1328-L1405), is selected when the flag is on. It builds HybridEP with 2L local experts, starts the planner in [`setup_metadata`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py#L1352-L1368), and in [`dispatch`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py#L1370-L1390) hands HybridEP the runtime IDs and the matching probabilities.
- `_HybridEPManager.dispatch` takes a new optional [`rank_capacity`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py#L1228-L1243) argument. Without it, behavior is unchanged. This is the one change to shared HybridEP code.
- Two no-op hooks, [`wrap_layer_input` and `finalize_layer_output`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py#L220-L226), are added to the dispatcher base class so the MoE layer can call them unconditionally.

### `megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py`

**Why:** the planner takes compact `[T, topk]` expert IDs. Building a `[T, E]` routing map and then compressing it would cost an extra kernel per layer.

**What changed:**
- With MoonEP on, the router returns compact int64 IDs and matching probabilities for every routing mode: top-k, hash, and quantile ([routing](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L997-L1045)).
- [`_dense_route_indices_dtype`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L486-L513) is restructured and now called for every routing mode. For the other backends it also excludes hash and sinkhorn, which preserves their previous behavior.

### `megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py`

**Why:** TE's grouped GEMM has to run over the natives plus the slots, but the slots must not be registered parameters. The FC2 gradient reduce also needs a trigger right after the FC2 weight-gradient GEMM so it can overlap FC1's backward.

**What changed:**
- [`bind_virtual_experts`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py#L439-L455) installs the slot weights as `weight{L..2L-1}` with `object.__setattr__`, which is how TE sees them while DDP and checkpointing don't.
- [`_VirtualExpertFC2WgradStore`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py#L237-L261) is installed as FC2's `wgrad_store`. TE then hands it the weight-gradient GEMM, which it runs immediately before starting the reduce.

### `megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py`

**Why:** the load balancer needs a hook on the layer input and output, and the shared experts need to run while the planner is in flight.

**What changed:**
- The layer binds the experts to the manager ([here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L387-L389)) and wraps the layer input ([here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L523)) and output ([here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L694)).
- With MoonEP on, the shared experts run after preprocess instead of before the router ([flag](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L207-L214), [reorder](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L740-L752)).

### `megatron/core/extensions/transformer_engine.py`

**Why:** `TEGroupedLinear` needs extra GEMM slots for the virtual experts, without changing initialization or the checkpoint layout.

**What changed:**
- `TEGroupedLinear` builds `num_gemms + num_virtual_experts` GEMMs ([here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/extensions/transformer_engine.py#L2707)).
- [`reset_parameters`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/extensions/transformer_engine.py#L2899-L2906) unregisters the slot weights before init, so no RNG is consumed for them and init matches a non-MoonEP model.
- `sharded_state_dict` covers only the owned GEMMs, so checkpoints are interchangeable ([here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/extensions/transformer_engine.py#L3010-L3032)).
- `is_first_microbatch` is forced to `None` whenever slots exist, because slot contents change between microbatches ([here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/extensions/transformer_engine.py#L2916-L2921)).

### `megatron/core/tensor_parallel/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py`, `gtp_cuda_graphs.py`

**Why:** with expert GTP, the push needs the gathered weights before TE consumes them, and the gradient reduce needs weight-gradient buffers that stay at a fixed address until the delayed reduce-scatter.

**What changed:**
- [`peek_group_for_{forward,backward}`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py#L2507-L2518) returns the gathered buffers without consuming them, issuing the all-gather itself if none is in flight ([`_peek_gathered_weight`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py#L1719-L1761)). To support this, the consume path no longer checks `next_w`/`prev_w is not None` ([fwd](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py#L1821-L1823), [bwd](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py#L1878-L1880)). This affects every GTP user, not just MoonEP.
- [`get_wgrad_tensor(persistent=True)`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py#L1996-L2015) returns a buffer from a fixed ring per domain ([`_bind_eager_wgrad_ring_slot`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py#L336-L360)), sized by the new `eager_wgrad_ring_size` knob. Before a buffer is reused, it waits for the previous reduce-scatter ([`_EagerWgradRingSlot`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py#L320-L333)).
- The ring helpers are factored out so the graph and eager rings share them ([`allocate_wgrad_ring`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/gtp_cuda_graphs.py#L248-L262)). [`wgrad_ring_key`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/gtp_cuda_graphs.py#L236-L245) now includes `chain_id`, so FC1 and FC2 get separate graph rings.

### Config / DDP / FSDP / teardown

**Why:** unsupported combinations should fail at startup, and the symmetric-memory windows must be released while the EP group is still alive.

**What changed:**
- `transformer_config.py`: the new [flag](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_config.py#L996-L997) (the CLI argument is auto-generated) and its [requirements check](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_config.py#L2236-L2318). Notable requirements: BF16 or native MXFP8, ETP=1, EP between 2 and 64, and only the whole-layer `moe` CUDA-graph scope ([here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_config.py#L3481-L3490)).
- DDP: MXFP8 requires `fp8_param_gather` and `reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag`, so that weight addresses stay fixed ([`_validate_config`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/distributed/distributed_data_parallel.py#L109-L123)).
- FSDP [v1](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/distributed/fsdp/mcore_fsdp_adapter.py#L192-L199) and [v2](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/distributed/fsdp/mcore_fsdp_adapter.py#L751-L758) raise an error when the flag is set.
- `destroy_model_parallel` calls `VirtualExpertLoadBalancer.finalize()` ([here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/megatron/core/parallel_state.py#L2586-L2595)).

## Tests

- **[`test_virtual_experts.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py)**:
  - [training parity](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L486) against plain HybridEP (EP2 with MTP, and EGTP2 with MXFP8): loss, gradients, and optimizer updates within tolerance over several steps;
  - [BF16 routing parity](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L791): outputs and dgrads bitwise, expert wgrads within tolerance (summation order differs);
  - [recompute](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L1018) and [offload scopes](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L1149);
  - [router output formats](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L1387);
  - config rejections ([topk](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L1330), [CUDA-graph scopes](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L1344), [layout](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L1361));
  - [GTP peek and ring behavior](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L168);
  - [barrier timeouts](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py#L1634).
- **[`test_moe_kernels.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py)**: the planner checked against a [CPU oracle](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py#L109) ([tie-breaks](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py#L234), [EP 1/2/4/8](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py#L382)), plus [CUDA-graph replay](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py#L399). Registered in the determinism [manifest](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py#L303).
- **[`test_te_wrappers.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_te_wrappers.py#L99)**: checkpoint and init parity.
- **[`test_token_dispatcher.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b25838d02c5ba0067b930e76540cc8de7f3d03a2/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_token_dispatcher.py#L52)**: a regression test for `rank_capacity`.

@@ -261,6 +261,7 @@ The table below covers every GTP-related CLI flag and Python knob. "Required" me
 | `async_reduction` | `True` | Async wgrad reduce-scatter; disable for easier debugging. |
 | `calculate_per_token_loss` | `False` | Must mirror `config.calculate_per_token_loss` (SUM vs MEAN RS). |
 | `graph_wgrad_ring_size` | `2` | Persistent wgrad ring slots per scheduling domain (§3.6). Increase if capture rejects same-key writers. |
+| `eager_wgrad_ring_size` | `2` | Persistent eager wgrad slots per scheduling/shape domain. Increase to delay buffer reuse at the cost of memory; set before the first backward. |
 
 ### 2.2 Required flags
 
@@ -329,7 +330,8 @@ At iter-0 you'll see one rank-0 log line confirming the active config:
 ```
 GTP_remat enabled. GTPRematConfig(pad_for_alignment=1, check_param_states=False,
   weight_prefetch=True, async_reduction=True, calculate_per_token_loss=False,
-  reduce_scatter_with_fp32_accumulation=False, graph_wgrad_ring_size=2)
+  reduce_scatter_with_fp32_accumulation=False, graph_wgrad_ring_size=2,
+  eager_wgrad_ring_size=2)
 ```
 
 (`pad_for_alignment=1` here because this example is BF16 with no quantization-tile
@@ -347,6 +349,7 @@ update_gtp_config(
     calculate_per_token_loss=False,  # Mirror config.calculate_per_token_loss (SUM vs MEAN RS)
     reduce_scatter_with_fp32_accumulation=False,  # wgrad RS: BF16 all-to-all + FP32 sum (§2.6)
     graph_wgrad_ring_size=2,      # Persistent wgrad slots per graph scheduling domain
+    eager_wgrad_ring_size=2,      # Persistent eager wgrad slots; independent of gather buffers
 )
 ```
 
@@ -873,6 +876,19 @@ The two modes differ only in release timing and the storage required to make ear
 
 The feature applies only to **local/partial CUDA graphs** and is enabled automatically. Full-iteration CUDA graphs do not use this feature because their backward execution has no local graph boundary.
 
+Eager callers that request persistent wgrad storage use a separate ring controlled by
+`eager_wgrad_ring_size` (default 2, minimum 1). On the first persistent-buffer request
+in a domain, all matching registered parameters are bound to fixed slots in registration
+order using the shared allocator and the same round-robin rule as CUDA graphs. Domains keep
+communication, shape, dtype, and expert index separate; grouped FC1 and FC2 have separate
+rings. Each domain allocates the smaller of the configured depth and its writer count.
+Before reuse, the previous owner finalizes any pending reduction and the compute stream
+waits on the slot's completion event. A deeper ring delays reuse and may improve overlap,
+at the cost of additional unsharded gradient buffers. It does not change gather-buffer
+double buffering, and a repeated backward for the same parameter still reuses its bound
+slot. Configure the depth before the first backward; `reset_gtp_state()` clears both the
+slots and their assignments.
+
 ### 3.7 Per-parameter alignment padding
 
 Low-precision tiling formats need each rank's local shard aligned to their tile size (MXFP8: 32, NVFP4: 16) — plain equal-sized AG/RS shards only need `dim0` divisible by `gtp_remat_size`, which padding is not required for (`_gtp_slice_one_param` skips it and just asserts that divisibility when `pad_for_alignment == 0`). BF16 has no tile-size requirement, so `training.py` sets `pad_for_alignment=1` for it — `dim0` still isn't guaranteed divisible by `gtp_remat_size` on its own, so padding stays on, just bounded to `gtp_remat_size - 1` rows instead of a 16/32-row tile margin. A weight's real `dim0` is rarely already a multiple of `pad_for_alignment × gtp_remat_size`, so `_gtp_slice_one_param` pads the *logical* tensor up to the next multiple before slicing it evenly across `gtp_remat_group` (§1.3) — the padding lands as a contiguous suffix of that padded buffer. It is real, allocated storage, but the wgrad GEMM only ever writes the logical prefix (§3.6), so it stays exact `0.0` for the life of the run: a permanent structural zero, not a value that merely happens to be zero.

@@ -106,6 +106,22 @@ class DistributedDataParallel(_BaseDataParallel):
 
     """
 
+    @staticmethod
+    def _validate_config(
+        config: TransformerConfig, ddp_config: DistributedDataParallelConfig
+    ) -> None:
+        """Validate model settings that depend on the data-parallel configuration."""
+        if config.moe_virtual_expert_load_balance and config.fp8:
+            if not ddp_config.fp8_param_gather:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "MoonEP with MXFP8 requires fp8_param_gather=True (--fp8-param-gather)."

+"""Persistent eager wgrad rings for Generalized Tensor Parallelism (GTP).
+
+Slots share the CUDA-graph ring allocation helpers and finalize their previous
+reduce-scatter reader before another eager writer reuses the storage.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Callable, Iterable
+
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.gtp_cuda_graphs import (
+    GraphWgradRingSlot,
+    allocate_wgrad_ring,
+    wgrad_ring_key,
+)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class EagerWgradRingSlot(GraphWgradRingSlot):
+    """Persistent eager input whose previous reduce-scatter must finish before reuse."""
+
+    rs_owner: object = None
+
+    def wait_for_reader(self) -> None:
+        """Finalize a deferred reduction before another GEMM writes into its input."""
+        rs_owner = self.rs_owner
+        if rs_owner is not None and rs_owner._wgrad_rs_handle is not None:
+            rs_owner._wait_reduce_scatter(finalize_grad=True)
+            # The previous result is accounted for; its marker must not suppress the next one.
+            rs_owner._already_finalized = False
+        self.ready_event.wait()
+
+
+_EAGER_WGRAD_RINGS: dict[tuple, list[EagerWgradRingSlot]] = {}
+
+
+def bind_eager_wgrad_ring_slot(
+    param, params: Iterable, *, ring_size: int, stream_key: Callable[[str, object], tuple]
+) -> EagerWgradRingSlot:
+    """Initialize a domain's registered writers together on its first persistent request."""
+    if ring_size < 1:
+        raise ValueError("GTP_CONFIG.eager_wgrad_ring_size must be at least 1")
+    key = wgrad_ring_key(param, stream_key)
+    if key not in _EAGER_WGRAD_RINGS:
+        matching_params = [
+            weight
+            for weight in params
+            if weight.requires_grad
+            and weight.chain_id == param.chain_id
+            and wgrad_ring_key(weight, stream_key) == key
+        ]
+        if not any(weight is param for weight in matching_params):
+            raise RuntimeError("Persistent eager wgrad writers must be registered in _GTP_PARAMS")
+        slots = _EAGER_WGRAD_RINGS[key] = allocate_wgrad_ring(
+            matching_params, key=key, ring_size=ring_size, slot_type=EagerWgradRingSlot
+        )
+        for param_index, weight in enumerate(matching_params):
+            weight._gtp_eager_wgrad_ring_slot = slots[param_index % len(slots)]
+    return param._gtp_eager_wgrad_ring_slot
+
+
+def clear_eager_wgrad_rings() -> None:
+    """Drop eager ring storage when the process-global GTP state is reset."""
+    _EAGER_WGRAD_RINGS.clear()

+#### Virtual-expert load balancing
+
+Enable with `--moe-token-dispatcher-type flex --moe-flex-dispatcher-backend hybridep
+--moe-virtual-expert-load-balance`. MoonEP balances overloaded experts by temporarily copying
+selected experts to other EP ranks. The planner uses the algorithm from
+[MoonshotAI/MoonEP](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/MoonEP); the integration here combines custom
+Triton kernels, a virtual-expert dispatcher, and Transformer Engine's grouped expert computation.
+
+- **Dispatcher:** Flex selects `_VirtualExpertHybridEPManager` in
+  [token_dispatcher.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/megatron/core/transformer/moe/token_dispatcher.py), which extends the existing HybridEP manager with
+  `VirtualExpertLoadBalancer`. It accepts the router's `[tokens, topk]` expert IDs and
+  probabilities, starts planning and weight prefetch, then supplies remapped runtime expert
+  IDs to HybridEP. HybridEP handles token dispatch and combine using a fixed receive capacity
+  calculated to cover the balanced workload and padding.
+- **Triton kernels:** [virtual_expert_triton.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/megatron/core/transformer/moe/ops/virtual_expert_triton.py) implements planning,
+  selected-weight prefetch, and replica-gradient reduction. The planner combines histogram
+  construction, cross-rank histogram exchange, placement, and route remapping in one cooperative
+  kernel launch. Separate transport kernels push selected weights into peer virtual slots and
+  read replica gradients back into their owners' native gradients through NCCL symmetric memory.
+  These kernels move expert weights and gradients; token movement remains with HybridEP.
+- **Expert buffers:** [virtual_expert_load_balancer.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/megatron/core/transformer/moe/virtual_expert_load_balancer.py) binds
+  native weights and temporary virtual slots into the FC1/FC2 runtime weight lists consumed by
+  TE's grouped GEMMs. Compatible layers share persistent weight and gradient arenas, reusing
+  replica storage across layers. Non-GTP native gradients accumulate directly into DDP buffers;
+  GTP natives use stable wgrad buffers acquired through TE's `DistributedWeight` interface.
+- **Execution and backward:** Autograd hooks coordinate planning, weight prefetch, and gradient
+  reduction on separate CUDA streams, with events establishing dependencies on expert compute.
+  Each forward retains its placement for backward, which refreshes replica weights before the
+  expert GEMMs. FC2 replica-gradient reduction can start as soon as its wgrad is ready, followed
+  by FC1. At the MoE input-backward boundary, compute waits for both replica reductions before
+  handing gradients to DDP or expert GTP.
+
+The router's logical expert selections and probabilities are preserved; remapping changes where
+the selected experts execute. Replica gradients return to the original parameters, which retain
+optimizer and checkpoint ownership. Replicas have no separate optimizer state.
+
+Requirements and limits:
+
+- Triton 3.5 or newer is required for launch-scoped descriptor allocation.
+- Use EP sizes 2–64, up to 8,192 experts evenly divided across EP ranks, top-k from 1 to
+  min(32, number of experts), and expert tensor parallel size 1.
+- All layers must share one EP topology. Local token counts must be equal across EP ranks and
+  remain fixed after each layer's first forward.
+- Use per-expert parameters with grouped-tensor GEMM, fused gradient accumulation, FP32 router
+  probabilities, and BF16 or native MXFP8 weights. The op fuser is optional. MXFP8 additionally
+  requires `--fp8-param --fp8-param-gather --reuse-grad-buf-for-mxfp8-param-ag` with the
+  `mxfp8` recipe and `e4m3` format.
+- Use regular DDP or the distributed optimizer with eagerly allocated expert `main_grad` buffers.
+  Megatron-FSDP v1/v2 and lazy gradient allocation are unsupported. Expert GTP is supported.
+- Leave `moe_expert_rank_capacity_factor` unset and disable `moe_paged_stash`. MoonEP selects
+  static-capacity HybridEP transport and calculates its own dropless budget, including padding.
+  Token dropping and expert capacity limits are unsupported.
+- Use `moe_hybridep_routing_map_mode='indices'` (the default) and a HybridEP build supporting
+  `topk_idx`. MoonEP routers return selected expert IDs and probabilities directly. If TE
+  cannot emit expert IDs, routing uses the unfused implementation.
+- Sinkhorn routing and DeepSeek-style expert bias (`--moe-router-enable-expert-bias`) are
+  unsupported. For CUDA graphs, use the whole-layer `moe` scope rather than `moe_router` or
+  `moe_preprocess`. Full/whole-MoE recomputation is unsupported. FC1 CPU offload currently
+  requires a separate HybridEP/TE capacity-buffer fix; MoE activation and fused-MLP offload
+  have test coverage.
+
+Supported routing includes FP32 sigmoid scores, router fusion, hash routing, `seq_aux_loss`, and quantile
+balancing with its own bias update. For `micro_batch` quantile balancing, set
+`--moe-router-load-balancing-type quantile_balancing --moe-aux-loss-coeff 0`, omit
+`--moe-router-enable-expert-bias` and `--moe-router-fusion`, and disable
+`--moe-router-force-load-balancing`. Quantile balancing requires token-count × top-k divisible
+by the expert count and does not support padding masks or group-limited routing.
+
+Virtual-expert gradients use FP32 storage and transport by default. With `--grad-reduce-in-bf16`,
+native and replica partial gradients are stored in BF16, added locally in FP32, then downcast once.
+BF16 partial storage can lose small cancellation residuals and increase optimizer-update differences;
+later FP32 addition cannot recover those residuals. To retain FP32 accumulation in subsequent
+reductions, enable `--ddp-reduce-scatter-with-fp32-accumulation` and, with expert GTP,
+`--gtp-remat-reduce-scatter-with-fp32-accumulation`.
+
+MoonEP's peer handshakes and cooperative-grid barriers time out after approximately 100 seconds
+of polling, including when `TRITON_DEBUG=0`. A timeout aborts the kernel and surfaces as an
+asynchronous CUDA launch failure; restart the affected processes. Other ranks still waiting in
+these barriers time out independently. This does not cover unrelated collectives or stalled
+GPU instructions.
+
+Training parity and supported offload/recompute cases are covered in
+`tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_virtual_experts.py`. Planner correctness and CUDA graph
+replay are covered in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py`; checkpoint
+loading and initialization parity are covered by
+`test_te_grouped_linear_virtual_expert_checkpoint` in the neighboring `test_te_wrappers.py`.
+
 ### Upcycling
 Use `--moe-use-upcycling` to enable upcycling, which loads the dense model from the `--load` directory, converts it to an MoE model at runtime, and starts training. The converted model is saved to the `--save` path before training begins. Upcycling is built on distributed checkpointing, supporting parallel modes different from existing dense checkpoints, such as arbitrary expert parallelism during upcycling.
